item.title: Clallam board approves $1M grant for Clallam Bay/Sekiu sewer project
item.description: Opportunity Fund dollars to be repaid to county general fund

item.title: State treasurer to speak at annual EDC banquet
item.description: Awards presentations slated for business, nonprofit, leader of year

item.title: One giant leap
item.description: Linda Christie of Port Townsend engages her 8-year-old rescue dog, Flaco, in a bit of gymnastic exercise at Fort Worden State Park. Flaco was mostly skin and bone when Christie rescued him from the streets of Mexico about five years ago, she said.

item.title: One dies, three injured in collision involving transit bus
item.description: PORT LUDLOW — A head-on traffic collision involving two passenger vehicles and a Jefferson Transit bus resulted in a fatality, a patient in critical condition and others injured on the scene.

item.title: STATE 1B TOURNAMENT: Neah Bay boys in the quarterfinals
item.description: SPOKANE — The Neah Bay boys basketball team will finish somewhere in the top eight of the state after beating Sunnyside Christian 74-58 in a Round of 12 1B state tournament game Wednesday morning at the Numerica Veterans Arena in Spokane.

item.title: Port Townsend man dies after October collision
item.description: PORT TOWNSEND — A 77-year-old Port Townsend man who was involved in a collision on state Highway 20 last October has died, the State Patrol reported.

item.title: Man sentenced to 10 years after pleading guilty to drug crimes
item.description: PORT ANGELES — A Port Angeles man has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after he pleaded guilty to multiple charges in Clallam County Superior Court.

item.title: STATE BASKETBALL: Rough time for Riders in Yakima’s SunDome against ATM
item.description: YAKIMA — Beaten badly on the boards, Port Angeles put up a fight defensively but still made a quick exit from the Class 2A state girls basketball tournament in a 53-29 loss to No. 5-seed Archbishop Thomas Murphy on Wednesday at the Yakima Valley SunDome.

item.title: NWAC MEN’S TOURNAMENT: Pirates lose in opener
item.description: PASCO — The Peninsula College men’s basketball team rallied early in the second half, but simply couldn’t overcome a huge rebounding gap in an 81-61 loss to Treasure Valley in the opening round of the Northwest Athletic Conference tournament.

item.title: WEST COAST LEAGUE: 19 WCL alumni to play in World Baseball Classic
item.description: PORTLAND, Ore. — The 2026 World Baseball Classic that began this week will feature 19 West Coast League alumni with representation on nine of the 20 teams in the event.
